task: Swap the transciphering symmetric cipher HERA -> Rubato, re-measure, cross-arm comparison (Prof. Debranjan's assigned task, branch rubato-swap).
status_tags_legend: CONFIRMED-RAN = executed this session, command given. CONFIRMED-SOURCE = verified against ckks_fv source (file+line) or a cited paper. UNVERIFIED = plausible, not independently checked this session.

machine_state.caveat: Absolute latencies below are NOT comparable to any number measured in a different session (PROJECT_STATE.md measurement rules). Same-session paired ratios (HERA vs Rubato, at fixed lane counts) are the defensible output; both ciphers were measured back-to-back in this session under identical machine state.

gate_b_resource_usage.description: Toy-scale (LogN=10) wall time and peak RSS for the two exact-parity harnesses (hera_r5_128as, rubato_128L), measured via a separate compiled test binary run with /proc/<pid>/status VmHWM polled every 0.1s (GNU time -v not installed on this host, no root to add it -- same documented substitution as the original 275 MB figure in toy_correctness/README.md). This is the ONLY server-side (homomorphic-evaluation) evidence available for either cipher while vendor_server's BFV eval is stub-only -- it is a TOY-SCALE (LogN=10, ~1/64th the ring degree of the real LogN=16 params) proxy, not a full-scale measurement, and must not be compared to the full-scale HERA figure below or used to project full-scale Rubato cost by simple scaling.

toy_vs_hera_ratio.note: Rubato's toy-scale run takes ~1.4x the wall time and ~2.1x the peak RSS of HERA's. Plausible drivers, not independently isolated this session: Rubato's larger block size (64 vs 16 ciphertext states carried through the FV evaluator) and its blocksize-64 linear layer (more ciphertext additions per round than HERA's 16-element one) -- NOT its Gaussian noise, since mfvRubato (the homomorphic evaluator) does not add noise (see cipher/rubato.go's package doc). Toy-scale numbers at LogN=10 do not necessarily scale linearly to LogN=16 -- treat as a directional signal only.

gate_b_resource_usage.full_scale_hera_reference_not_directly_c: PROJECT_STATE.md records a full-scale (LogN=16, real secure params) hera.Crypt run: 73.7s, peak VmHWM 9.54GB. That is a DIFFERENT measurement (full ring degree, not LogN=10 toy) and must not be divided against or combined with the toy-scale figures above. No equivalent full-scale run exists for Rubato.

axis_b_hera_vs_rubato_client_cipher.description: Client-side plaintext-path benchmark (tools/transciphering/bench, --cipher=hera|rubato), 256 features/transaction, n=200 measured + 10 warmup per point, HERA and Rubato run back-to-back this session under the machine_state above.

cipher_config.hera: HERA-16: m=16, r=5, t=2^26 -- SHAKE256(nonce)-derived round keys, fixed [2,3,1,1] circulant linear layer (both replacing the prior fixed-table/AES-ECB-PRF implementation)
cipher_config.rubato: Rubato-128L: n=64, r=2, q=0x1fc0001, sigma=1.6356633496458739795537788457309656607510203877762320964302959 -- SHAKE256(nonce||counter)-derived round keys, blocksize-64 linear layer, sequential Feistel-square nonlinear layer, client-side Gaussian noise

axis_b_hera_vs_rubato_client_cipher.headline: Rubato-128L client encrypt costs ~1.75-2.25x HERA-16 (mean), ~1.7-2.1x (median), consistently across the 1-16 lane sweep this session. Treat this range, not a single point estimate, as the result -- see machine_state caveat. This is a PER-RECORD ratio; see per_element_normalization below for the per-keystream-element view.
axis_b_hera_vs_rubato_client_cipher.upload_size_finding: Upload size in bytes is IDENTICAL between HERA and Rubato at every lane count (both use the same OnlineCiphertextBytes(n) = 4n+28 wire format) -- the cipher swap changes client CPU cost only, not the ~16x-249x upload-size reduction vs plain CKKS standard (262,257 bytes) that motivated using a symmetric cipher at all.

per_element_normalization.description: HERA-16 yields HeraStateSize=16 usable keystream elements per block; Rubato-128L yields RubatoOutputSize=60 (RubatoBlockSize=64 minus the 4-element truncation, fv_rubato.go/RtF_bench_test.go's state[0:blocksize-4]). The by_lane_count ratios above are per-RECORD (fixed at 256 features), which is invariant to this yield difference by construction (dividing both cipher's time by the same n cancels it out). This section instead isolates single-block cost via a dedicated Go micro-benchmark (cipher/block_bench_test.go: BenchmarkHERABlock, BenchmarkRubatoBlock, go test ./cipher/... -bench . -benchtime=2000x -run '^$'), excluding AEAD-wrap overhead and multi-block batching effects present in the per-record numbers above, then divides by each cipher's per-block yield.
per_element_normalization.headline: Per keystream element (not per record), Rubato-128L costs ~3.05x HERA-16 with its Gaussian noise step included (what Encrypt() actually does) but only ~1.19x with noise excluded. ~61% of Rubato's per-block client cost in THIS implementation is the Gaussian noise sampler (cipher/rubato.go's noiseAGN, which draws from crypto/rand per sample) -- once that's excluded, Rubato's larger-state arithmetic is nearly at parity with HERA's per element. This is specific to this module's own AGN implementation choice (crypto/rand-backed Box-Muller with rejection sampling), not an inherent property of Rubato's algebraic structure -- a faster CSPRNG-seeded (not per-draw crypto/rand) sampler would likely close most of this gap. The per-record ratio (2.10x mean, lanes=1) and the with-noise per-element ratio (3.05x) differ because per-record divides a small n=256 by many blocks (16 for HERA, 5 for Rubato with truncation waste) using coarser (µs-resolution, time.Now()-based) batch timing; the per-block micro-benchmark uses go test's more precise ns-resolution timing on an isolated single block.

multiplicative_depth_argument.description: The client-side numbers above measure PLAINTEXT arithmetic cost, which is not what determines homomorphic (server-side, FHE) evaluation cost. FHE cost is dominated by multiplicative depth -- the number of SEQUENTIALLY-DEPENDENT ciphertext-ciphertext multiplications (each needing relinearization and consuming noise budget), not by how many total arithmetic operations a plaintext CPU performs. See tools/transciphering/README.md's 'Multiplicative depth' section for the full argument; summary here.
multiplicative_depth_argument.hera_depth: 5 rounds x degree-3 cube S-box (x -> x^3 = x^2 . x). Each cube is 2 SEQUENTIAL ciphertext multiplications (fv_hera.go:355-363: x2=Mul(ct,ct); Relin; x3=Mul(x2,ct); Relin). 5 cube() calls total (4 in the round loop + 1 in finalization) x 2 mults each = 10 multiplicative levels.
multiplicative_depth_argument.rubato_128L_depth: 2 rounds x degree-2 Feistel-square (state[i] += state[i-1]^2). Each feistel() call squares blocksize-1=63 DIFFERENT, mutually-independent state elements (fv_rubato.go:734-741) -- these are logically PARALLEL, not sequentially dependent, so one feistel() call costs exactly 1 multiplicative level regardless of state size. 2 feistel() calls total (1 in the round loop + 1 in finalization) x 1 mult level each = 2 multiplicative levels.
multiplicative_depth_argument.implication: By this depth count, Rubato-128L's homomorphic evaluation should require ~5x fewer sequential ciphertext multiplications than HERA-16's, which is the entire design rationale behind Rubato's noise mechanism (Ha et al., Eurocrypt 2022): trade a few extra rounds/client-side noise sampling for a much shallower homomorphic circuit. The client-side measurements in this artifact (axis_b, per_element_normalization) do NOT test this at all -- they measure plaintext CPU cost, dominated in Rubato's case by this module's own noise-sampling implementation, an entirely different cost driver than ciphertext multiplicative depth.
multiplicative_depth_argument.deciding_comparison_status: BLOCKED. The actual homomorphic-evaluation cost comparison (mfvHera.Crypt vs mfvRubato.Crypt wall time, at full or even toy scale with proper timing instrumentation) is the measurement that would confirm or refute this depth argument, and it has not been done at full scale (vendor_server's BFV eval is stub-only) or precisely at toy scale (gate_b_resource_usage above gives whole-test wall time/RSS for the full HalfBoot pipeline, not isolated Crypt()-call timing per cipher). This remains the single most important open measurement for this task's stated goal of a cross-arm comparison.

axis_c_simd_circuit_behaviour.description: Client-cipher lane sweep (1/4/8/16, matching hhe_breakeven.json's batch_occupancy_lanes axis) is covered by axis_b above for both ciphers. What's NOT covered: SIMD lane behavior of the homomorphic (server-side) evaluation path (mfvHera.Crypt / mfvRubato.Crypt across many simultaneous FV-slot lanes) -- the toy harnesses above only exercise slot 0 (HERA) / output-element 0 (Rubato), proving correctness of one lane, not throughput across many. That remains PENDING, same blocker as axis_a below.

known_defects_fixed_this_task: cipher/hera.go: replaced the fixed heraRC table (whose 5th row was an admitted, unsourced placeholder) and heraRoundKey's AES-128-ECB PRF with SHAKE256(nonce)-derived round keys (roundKeys, shared with rubato.go), matching ckks_fv's fv_hera.go:100-113 / RtF_bench_test.go:500-513 exactly.
cipher/hera.go: replaced heraMixColumns (which derived its matrix from heraRC per round -- never matched HERA's actual spec) with the fixed [2,3,1,1] circulant from RtF_bench_test.go:525-547.
cipher/hera.go: replaced the fabricated nonce-mixed initial state (nonce[i%16]+ctr*(i+1)) with HERA's actual fixed public initial state (i+1), matching fv_hera.go:65-68.

cipher/hera.go: restructured encryptBlock's round order to match the reference exactly (initial whitening, then linLayer+cube+addRoundKey per round, finalization with a double linLayer) -- the prior structure (addRoundKey+cube+mix interleaved per round) did not match.

sourcing.rubato_variant_choice: Rubato-128L (RUBATO128L: n=64, r=2, q=0x1fc0001, sigma=1.6356633496458739795537788457309656607510203877762320964302959 -- fv_rubato.go:48-53). Grassi et al. (CRYPTO 2023, eprint 2023/822 Section 6.1/7.1, p.22, read directly this task) state the attack's bound 'cannot be established' for Rubato-128L specifically, unlike the other five variants. This means Rubato-128L is NOT COVERED by this attack's established bound -- not the same as proven secure. This benchmark is a performance/feasibility comparison, not a security endorsement.
sourcing.constants_not_fabricated: Every cipher constant, matrix coefficient, and derivation formula used in cipher/hera.go and cipher/rubato.go is cited in-code to an exact ckks_fv file/line at the pinned SHA 105fc73115b56f1d6ff357029c7682b19a6d8510. The previous 'Table 3 of Cho et al. 2021' citation for heraRC was discarded, not re-sourced or replaced with another placeholder.
